feature: Marketing Free Scan Remediate step (/scan/remediate) — Git #1375, Phase of Feature #1352. Step 5 of 5: a real, narrowly-scoped write-consent gate recreated from the confirmed design's {{ writeStage }} block (Design/marketing/marketing_handoff/Marketing Checkout.dc.html), followed by the real findings-driven remediation guide. The Graph application permissions on the consent card are DERIVED per Prospect from the phases they actually bought in the Review step (#1374) through their own scan's open findings, the active config packs that fix them, and those packs' real Graph writes — never a fixed list and never a fixture. Served by routes/public-free-scan-remediate.ts -> lib/free-scan-write-scopes.ts + lib/remediation-checklist.ts.
notes: SCOPE OF THIS MANIFEST — what is deterministically assertable from a browser and an HTTP client:
1. The identity and payment gates on all four /api/public/free-scan/remediate/* routes
(apiTests). Every one is unauthenticated on purpose — a Free Scan Prospect is never issued
a JWT (#656), and paying for a SOW does not create one — so each resolves the tenant only
from a live checkout sessionId or an emailed fsr_ return token, exactly as #1358/#1359/#1374
already do. These assert the real refusal codes for a missing credential, a malformed
sessionId, a well-formed-but-unknown sessionId and a bogus return token.
2. That the Remediate page renders the shared flow strip with Remediate as the CURRENT step and
Consent/Scan/Results/Review already ticked (uiSteps). This is #1375's scope item 6 and it
holds with no credential at all, because the strip renders above everything else.
3. That a visitor with no free-scan session gets the honest 'we lost track of your scan' state
rather than a consent screen with nothing behind it.
WHAT IS NOT ASSERTED HERE, and why:
The write-consent screen itself and the guide behind it need a real consented tenant with a
completed scan AND a signed, paid engagement — none of which a browser can mint here, since the
read consent is granted in a popup on Microsoft's own domain and the payment goes through
Stripe's cross-origin Payment Element. Faking a session to reach those screens would be coverage
of a fixture, not of the product. Both halves are covered instead against live Postgres:
artifacts/api-server/src/lib/free-scan-write-scopes.live-db.test.ts — seeds a scratch Prospect
with real findings on two pillars and asserts the derivation: only permissions the write app
genuinely requests appear, each carries the real phase and real check key behind it, deferring
a phase drops that phase's permissions, a bought phase with nothing executable is named
honestly, and the asked/beyond-scope lists partition the registration exactly.
artifacts/api-server/src/routes/public-free-scan-remediate.live-db.test.ts — asserts the gates
end to end: an unpaid engagement and a tenant with no read grant are both refused BEFORE any
consent_invite_tokens row exists; a decline never touches tenants.consent.writeBack; the
checklist claim lands in remediation_tracker_steps keyed by checkKey under the real customerId;
and the happy path mints exactly one HMAC-bound, single-use consent URL aimed at this tenant.
The Microsoft admin-consent screen is Microsoft's own page and is never driven from here. The
grant is only ever recognised through the shared, unchanged /api/admin/write-consent/callback,
which requires Microsoft to actually issue a write-app token for the tenant first (#4197).
